newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth seeks Florida long-distance nod.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth seeks Florida long-distance nod.

text.p: BellSouth Corp said on Monday it asked the Florida Public Service Commission to let it fully compete in the long-distance market.
If Florida approves its bid, BellSouth would seek final U.S. Federal Communications Commission approval to compete with such long-distance companies as AT&T Corp and MCI Communications Corp.

BellSouth said in a news release that 102 companies have been certified to enter the local telephone service market in Florida. That should entitle BellSouth to be allowed to compete with long-distance companies, it said.

"The intent of the Telecommunications Bill (of 1996) was for local telephone companies to enter the long distance market as close as possible to the time when long distance companies enter the local market," BellSouth-Florida President Joseph Lacher said in the release. "Well, despite what you've been hearing from those trying to delay our entry into long-distance, local market competition is alive, well and growing here in Florida."
Florida Public Service Commission hearings on BellSouth's request were scheduled for September, with a decision due in early November.
